findings.highlight: Even if Saber doesn’t want to, I’ll have to forcefully pull her back and bring her home
findings.evidenceJa: 危険だと判断したら即座に撤退するだけだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou resolves simply to retreat immediately if he judges the situation dangerous.
findings.explanation: The non-Realta branch restores a commented-out plan to drag Saber home against her will, adding a concrete coercive action absent from the active Japanese.

findings.highlight: the Master at the Ryuudou Temple and us, the intruders
findings.evidenceJa: 柳洞寺に潜むマスターと、その陣地に挑む俺
findings.governingReading: The figurative scale assigns the two possible deaths to the hidden Master and Shirou himself.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Shirou with the whole intruding pair, blurring the mortal opposition Saber has just stated.

findings.highlight: at the end of the winding mountain path
findings.evidenceJa: 緩やかな山道の終わり
findings.governingReading: The temple stands at the end of a gently sloping mountain road.
findings.explanation: The English changes gradient into winding shape.

findings.highlight: The road leading up to the remarkably tall mountain
findings.governingReading: The long stairs lead toward the mountainside of one of Fuyuki’s most prominent heights.
findings.explanation: The English makes the road lead to the mountain generally and omits the specific mountainside destination.

findings.highlight: This place was an ominous place last time, but it is worse now.
findings.governingReading: Saber says the wind is unfavorable and orders Shirou not to leave her side.
findings.explanation: The English conditionally restores an inactive comparison with a previous visit, adding history and escalation absent from the active Japanese.

findings.highlight: There must be something wrong about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 何か、その監視役とやらに思うところがあるのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether Saber has some concern about the supposed familiar.
findings.explanation: The English turns his open reading of her expression into an asserted defect in the familiar.

findings.highlight: There are two reasons the watcher would depart
findings.evidenceJa: 門番を下げた意味は二つ
findings.governingReading: The enemy has deliberately withdrawn the gatekeeper despite knowing of their arrival.
findings.explanation: “Depart” removes the unseen enemy’s agency in pulling the guard back, weakening the trap logic.

findings.highlight: nothing will happen until we see their faces
findings.evidenceJa: 相手の顔を見ない事には始まらない
findings.governingReading: They cannot begin to assess or deal with the opponent without first confronting them.
findings.explanation: The English copies the face idiom literally and implies events themselves cannot occur.

findings.governingReading: Saber turns back, her golden hair marking the visual beat.
findings.explanation: The English makes her hair the grammatical agent of turning.

findings.evidenceJa: この時代において転移魔術だと
findings.governingReading: Saber is shocked that transference magecraft exists in the modern age.
findings.explanation: The English again collapses 魔術 into generic magic in a technical identification.

findings.highlight: Saber charges forward to grab my hand.
findings.evidenceJa: 地を蹴って俺の腕を掴むセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber kicks off the ground and actually grabs Shirou’s arm before Rider knocks her away.
findings.explanation: The English changes arm to hand and renders the completed grasp as an attempted purpose.

findings.highlight: the sickness is as if I’m another living thing
findings.evidenceJa: 別の生物になったような嘔吐感
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels vomiting nausea as though his body has become another organism.
findings.explanation: The English produces an incoherent simile and loses the bodily transformation sensation.

findings.highlight: There’s no blood left in my body
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese fragments Shirou’s perception around his fingers, cold, darkness, and failing consciousness.
findings.explanation: The mature branch replaces that sequence with inactive blood-loss narration absent from the active witness.

findings.highlight: With such weak abilities, you have no value even as a slave
findings.evidenceJa: そんな低能では奴隷にする価値もない
findings.governingReading: Caster calls Shirou such an imbecile or low intellect that he is worthless even as a slave.
findings.explanation: The English changes her contempt for his intelligence into an assessment of weak combat ability.

findings.evidenceJa: 令呪を切り取っていく
findings.governingReading: The distorted dagger cuts away Shirou’s Command Spells.
findings.explanation: The mature branch changes removal of the Command Spells into amputation of his entire left arm.
